name: Cross-Asset Regime
rationale: Cross-asset regime rules use another market, such as bonds, volatility, credit, or rates, to condition equity exposure.
expected_benefit: Better behavior during equity declines if external markets provide useful stress signals.
failure_modes: Regime signals that lag the equity move.

canonical_variants.name: Bond-trend equity filter
canonical_variants.description: Condition equity exposure on the trend of a bond ETF or Treasury proxy.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A bond-trend regime filter may improve equity drawdown behavior during rate-sensitive stress periods.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 75% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Volatility-proxy equity filter
canonical_variants.description: Reduce equity exposure when a volatility proxy enters a stressed regime.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A volatility-proxy equity filter may reduce crash exposure without overly reducing normal-market exposure.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 25% relative and avoid worse Sharpe.

canonical_variants.name: Credit-spread proxy filter
canonical_variants.description: Use risky-credit versus Treasury behavior as an equity-risk signal.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A credit-stress proxy may identify equity-risk-off regimes before price-only equity filters react.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown without failing return retention below 70% of benchmark CAGR.

suggested_validation: Audit calendar alignment before any performance interpretation.
Use a single external signal first.
Prespecify whether the objective is drawdown control or return enhancement.
execution_notes: The current single-strategy schema cannot reference another symbol as a signal input.
